entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT JABALPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is the third application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.168/2022 dated 21.6.2022 registered at Police Station Lidhora District Tikamgarh for the offence under Sections 379, 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC and Section 15(2) and 16 of the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962.

entities.text: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Earlier two bail applications of the applicant were dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 17.11.2022 passed in M.Cr.C. No.49855/2022 and order dated 13.12.2022 passed in M.Cr.C. No.57679/2022.

As per the prosecution story on 21.6.2022 Akhilesh Tiwari, Senior Manager, Bharat Petroleum Refinery, Bina, lodged an FIR stating that an underground 18 inch steel pipeline has been laid from Bina refinery to Kanpur.
It passes through village Ishon (Mathol) Police Station Lidhora.
For the safety of pipeline, daily patrolling is being done by guards of SIS Ltd. Company.
Patrolling time is from 10.00 P.M. night to 8.A.M. in the morning.
In the intervening night of 20-21.6.2022 Guard Karan Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36860848/
1 Bhanu Pratap and Gun man Sanjay Jha were on patrolling.
At around 2.30 A.M. when they reached near Lidhora, they received an alarm message about Pipeline near Ishon.
When they reached near pipeline at Ishon, they found a tanker bearing registration No. 13 AW 3749 parked there.
Seeing them tanker driver and other unidentified persons fled away from the spot.

When they checked the tanker, they found that accused have stolen almost 18 KL diesel from pipeline by making a hole in the pipeline and by fitting valve and a green colour plastic pipe of 10 meter by drilling the pipeline.
They had stolen 18 thousand liters diesel worth Rs.15,30,000/-.
FIR was registered and tanker was seized.
After investigation charge sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is the driver of the tanker.
He was not aware about theft of diesel from pipeline.

It is further submitted that learned trial Court has framed charges only for commission of offence under Section 379 and 420/34 of IPC and Section 15(2) of The Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962.

entities.text: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Only the offence under Section 15(2) of the Act is punishable with 10 years R.I.
As trial of the case will take considerable time, applicant may be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail.

It is a case where applicant along with others not only made hole in the steel pipeline of the oil refinery but have also stolen 18000 liters diesel worth Rs.15,30,000/- as same was found filled in the tanker.
It is not a simple case of theft.
Drilling of pipeline of oil refinery may endanger the life of thousands of people in the locality.
Therefore, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, including the gravity of offence, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
Therefore, this third bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the applicant - Karan Singh is dismissed.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE mrs. mishra Karan Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36860848/
